output.title: Transcript Accuracy Is a Workflow Cost
output.body:
If transcript accuracy matters to your business, the useful question is not “is AI good enough?” It is: which recurring transcript task costs you more friction today — manual checking, or accepting a draft that still needs review?

Treat accuracy as a bounded workflow decision. First separate the use case: customer-facing meeting notes, internal call summaries, or text pulled from invoices and other records. Each has a different tolerance for error. For any high-risk decision, human approval stays in the loop. Money movement and other high-risk approvals should stay human.

The practical next step is simple: pick one transcript task that repeats every week, then note two things for your own records — how long verification takes, and what a single mistake forces you to fix. That gives you a real threshold instead of a vague feeling that “the transcript looked fine.” Fine is not a control.

If the task is low risk, a draft may be enough. If it affects customer communication or approvals, you need a tighter review step. Bareni currently keeps medical, legal, and high-sensitivity financial work out of scope as a matter of discipline, not because those workflows can never be automated.

Choose one recurring transcript workflow, measure the verification burden, and decide whether AI should stay a draft or become part of the process.
